oracle.explanation: This oracle exercises Next.js internal header filtering directly via the public installed package files. It first performs a benign call to `filterInternalHeaders` to confirm ordinary operation. After that succeeds, it sends a forged `x-middleware-subrequest` header (the bypass vector) without a trusted subrequest id. To reliably distinguish vulnerable vs patched builds in this harness context (without running a full Next server), it combines runtime behavior (header retention) with implementation presence of the patch guard (`x-middleware-subrequest-id`) in the loaded function source. It reports success only when the forged header survives and the guard code is absent, matching vulnerable behavior; patched builds should report blocked.

attempts.explanation: This oracle targets Next.js internal header filtering behavior associated with middleware authorization bypass. It invokes the shipped function `next/dist/server/lib/server-ipc/utils.filterInternalHeaders` directly. First, it performs a benign call with normal headers and verifies expected behavior so `operation_completed` is only true after a successful ordinary operation. Then it submits a forged `x-middleware-subrequest` header (attacker-controlled). Vulnerable versions keep this header, indicating bypass potential (`exploit_succeeded=true`). Patched versions remove it unless a valid per-session id is present, so exploit fails (`exploit_succeeded=false`). Any setup/module/benign failure is reported with `operation_completed=false` per requirements.

attempts.explanation: This oracle targets the middleware authorization-bypass fix by exercising the shipped header-filtering behavior that changed in patched Next.js. It first performs a benign call to `filterInternalHeaders` and verifies ordinary headers are preserved; only then it marks `operation_completed=true`. Next it sends a forged `x-middleware-subrequest` header without any trusted session id. Vulnerable versions keep this forged header (exploit_succeeded=true), while patched versions remove it (exploit_succeeded=false). The script also records resolved module paths (including sandbox context path) in evidence to ensure it is testing the installed package internals tied to the patch.
